This proves the population pin is what those steps actually assert against: moving the pin off the capture must break the audit, because if it did not the constant would be decoration and the population would once again be whatever the dataset's own header said it was. Origin: QA round 3 item H-G and framework gate-population D1/D2, where dropping a trailing epoch and doctoring the header to agree returned Conditional Pass, exit 0.

Before 2026-09-09 the epoch size was a bare literal 50 compared against seeds.length — both operands from inside the file being scored.

name: M30 QA-03 display multiplier reverts to float multiply-then-floor
find:
const cents = minesMultiplierDisplayCents(mineCount, tilesRevealed);
  return cents === null ? NaN : Number(cents) / 100;
guard: The defect QA-03 closed, re-armed as a registry entry. `Math.floor(multExact * 100)` understates 31 of the 300 reference cells by a cent — at m=1,k=10 the exact multiplier is 33/20 = 1.65 but the binary64 product lands on 1.6499999999999997 and floors to 1.64. Step 7 CANNOT see it: the 31 affected cells are all at reveal depths the capture never won at, so every captured `multiplier` field agrees under either arithmetic (3,104/3,104, measured). The guard that fires is Step 19, which re-derives outputs/audit-figures.json and compares it to the copy on disk — the reference grid is IN that artifact, so a change to the grid arithmetic is a change to the evidence. That is the point of the entry: it names the step that actually catches a defect the payout steps are blind to, so nobody later assumes Step 7 was covering this.
